Convivial

/kun-VIV-ee-ul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Convivial means characterized by feasting, drinking, and a merry, friendly social atmosphere.

The graduation dinner was a convivial affair, with heaping plates, clinking glasses, and laughter that carried into the street.

Worked Example

Every autumn, the whole block gathers in the Riveras' backyard for the harvest potluck. Tables sag under trays of tamales, casseroles, and pies, someone always brings a guitar, and neighbors linger over cups of hot cider trading stories until the porch lights come on. Even newcomers are pulled into the toasts and the laughter within minutes. By dessert, the convivial mood has turned a yard full of strangers and acquaintances into something like a family reunion.

The gathering's festive atmosphere of shared food, drink, and merry company is exactly what convivial describes.

How Convivial Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

festive

festive: cheerful and celebratory in mood

Antonyms

somber

somber: dark, gloomy, and serious

dreary

dreary: dull and cheerless

How Strong Is It? — cheerful → convivial → uproarious

cheerful vs. convivial

cheerful vs. convivial: A cheerful gathering simply has a light, happy mood, while a convivial one adds shared food, drink, and toasts to the merriment.

uproarious vs. convivial

uproarious vs. convivial: A convivial banquet is festive but still warm and sociable, while an uproarious one tips over into wild noise and near-chaos.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of convivial.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together, with

Root — viv

Root — viv: from Latin vivere, to live

Suffix — -ial

Suffix — -ial: a form of -al, characteristic of, pertaining to

Put it together

Put it together: Convivial comes from Latin convivium, 'a feast or banquet,' built from con- (together) plus vivere (to live): a feast is literally a place where people 'live together' around the table for an evening. The suffix -ial, a form of -al meaning 'characteristic of,' turns that banquet into an adjective describing any gathering with the festive character of a shared feast.

Use the root in a new word: revive

Use the root in a new word: revive: A splash of cold water helped revive the fainting runner, literally bringing her back to life, from the same Latin root vivere.

Word Choice

warm, appreciative register

Convivial describes the festive mood of an event or gathering built around shared food and drink (a convivial dinner party, a convivial reception, a convivial atmosphere). Use it for the spirit of the occasion itself rather than for one person's everyday personality.
